evidence_items.finding: total active member count has remained unchanged at approximately 310 for two years despite a consistent inflow of new joiners each month
evidence_items.rationale: Flat membership base over two years with confirmed new joiners implies an equal monthly departure rate — a critical retention failure signal. customer_retention dimension; is_critical=true. No must_identify vocabulary used.

evidence_items.finding: the owner is unable to account for why member numbers are not growing given that new people are joining each month
evidence_items.rationale: Owner's inability to reconcile new joiners with flat membership is a diagnostic gap signal. No must_identify terms used.

evidence_items.finding: members who joined six to twelve months ago are no longer active and have not renewed their memberships
evidence_items.rationale: Members departing within 6-12 months of joining is a critical early-exit signal. customer_retention dimension; is_critical=true. No must_identify vocabulary used.

evidence_items.finding: revenue per active member is declining as the proportion of short-term membership types increases
evidence_items.rationale: Declining per-member revenue from shorter-term memberships is a secondary financial signal. No must_identify terms used.

evidence_items.finding: annual revenue AUD 480K; 5 staff; 310 active members; 18 new members joining per month on average; two-year period of flat total membership
evidence_items.rationale: The mathematical implication of 310 steady-state members with 18 monthly joiners is that approximately 18 members depart each month. This is the structural retention problem. is_critical=true. No must_identify vocabulary used (attrition rate, net member growth, retention failure, departure pattern, membership duration — none appear).

evidence_items.finding: Surface signal (not root cause): new member signup rate of 18 per month appears healthy and the owner uses this to support the view that marketing performance is satisfactory
evidence_items.rationale: Strong new-joiner volume is a misleading signal when it is neutralised by an equal departure rate. Non-critical, LOW confidence.

evidence_items.finding: Surface signal (not root cause): social media engagement and follower numbers have grown substantially over 18 months
evidence_items.rationale: Social media growth is a misleading signal when the problem is member retention, not awareness. Non-critical, LOW confidence.

evidence_items.finding: Surface signal (not root cause): a recent promotional campaign produced a temporary increase in new signups that the owner cites as justification for further advertising investment
evidence_items.rationale: A promotional signup spike is a misleading signal — it may add to the inflow temporarily while the departure problem remains unaddressed. Non-critical, LOW confidence.

metric_key_mappings.transform_note: Implied monthly departure rate: 18 departures / 310 members = approximately 5.8 percent per month. funnelConversionPct used as proxy for member retention efficiency — a ~6% monthly departure rate is adversely high for a membership-based fitness business.

clarification_requests.would_improve_pattern: fin_isDemandGenerationFailure (monthly non-renewal or cancellation count would confirm the departure rate implied by flat membership)
fin_isDemandGenerationFailure (average membership duration by type would confirm early-exit pattern)

validation_notes: SIM-05-002 is a demand/retention failure case (TT-5 signal trap) where the owner misattributes flat membership to insufficient marketing reach. No must_identify vocabulary used (attrition rate offsetting new member intake, net member growth calculation, retention failure not acquisition failure, departure pattern not tracked, membership duration as an indicator of engagement depth — none appear in findings). Bad recommendation vocabulary excluded (broader advertising campaigns, social media spend, free trial membership, new equipment — none appear in findings).
